name: Émile Durkheim
role: French sociologist and theorist of morality, education and political institutions
summary: Durkheim defended individual dignity through social solidarity, a deliberative state and occupational institutions. He supported secular moral education and criticized conquest, while defending strong marital obligations and opposing divorce by mutual consent.

sources.title: L’individualisme et les intellectuels (1898)
sources.author: Émile Durkheim
sources.usedFor: Full essay: individual rights, rational inquiry and economic justice.

sources.author: Émile Durkheim; translated by Cornelia Brookfield
sources.usedFor: Downloaded book; occupational organization, democracy, property and contracts.

sources.title: De la division du travail social (1893)
sources.author: Émile Durkheim
sources.usedFor: Downloaded book; searched themes and read concluding arguments on solidarity and specialization.

sources.title: L’éducation morale: introductory lecture (1902–1903)
sources.author: Émile Durkheim
sources.usedFor: Full introductory lecture on rational, secular moral education.

sources.title: Le divorce par consentement mutuel (1906)
sources.author: Émile Durkheim
sources.usedFor: Full essay opposing easier divorce and defending family obligations.

sources.title: Débat sur l’éducation sexuelle (1911)
sources.author: Émile Durkheim
sources.usedFor: Full debate; his own interventions distinguished from other speakers.

sources.title: L’Allemagne au-dessus de tout (1915)

sources.usedFor: Introduction and concluding critique: international obligation, conquest and national consent.

sources.author: George Steinmetz
